response_change.child_relation: Introduce product rebinding/inhibition so the effective conversion of bound substrate depends on accumulated product P; then dP_dt at a given C decreases as P rises, creating history-dependent curvature in the rate trajectory during batch accumulation.

plan.activation_condition: Observable when product accumulates to a non-negligible fraction of the conserved substrate-derived pool during the monitored batch trajectory, so that P is no longer small compared with S + C + P and product binding can compete measurably with catalysis.
plan.train_hidden_contrast: In training, mild accumulation would show slight downward deviation from the parent's fixed dP_dt/C gain at late times; in holdout with larger initial substrate or longer observation, the same mechanism strengthens into clearer late-phase rate suppression as P grows.
plan.continuation_path: In the limit of vanishing product inhibition strength, or throughout regimes where P remains negligible, the model reduces continuously to dP_dt = k_cat*C with the original batch dynamics.
plan.promotion_reason: Reversible product inhibition requires tracking a product-bound inactive enzyme pool or equivalent dynamic occupancy; existing states S, C, and P do not contain that enzyme sequestration memory because free enzyme is currently fixed algebraically as E_total - C.
plan.gap_statement: The current model omits product inhibition/rebinding, so accumulated product cannot feed back on catalytic throughput during the same batch run.
plan.baseline_assumption: Relax the assumption that product neither rebinds nor affects forward catalysis; allow product to reversibly sequester enzyme in a nonproductive form.
plan.scientific_mechanism: Competitive or mixed product inhibition via reversible binding of product to free enzyme, reducing the free enzyme available for substrate association and therefore indirectly lowering product formation as P accumulates.
plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is product inhibition, common for enzyme reactions in closed batches once product accumulates. The parent target mapping has a fixed-environment shortcut: dP_dt depends only on C through one constant gain k_cat, so if C is supplied the scored mapping ignores whether product has accumulated. Varying initial substrate concentration while holding enzyme parameters and E_total fixed changes how much P builds up over the trajectory. Under the parent, a single refitted parameter set still enforces the same dP_dt-versus-C line across low- and high-product phases. Under the child, the same observed C yields lower dP_dt when P is large because some enzyme is trapped in a product-bound inactive pool, altering both target slope versus C and the late-time curvature of P accumulation. This contrast is scientifically admissible only when product reaches appreciable levels within the observed transient/depletion window; if product stays small, the refinement is weak and the parent is effectively recovered.

plan.continuation_path: In the low-product limit or large inhibition half-saturation limit, the refined inhibition law reduces to the parent’s mass-action-like dependence on P.
plan.gap_statement: The current model treats reversible product inhibition as indefinitely linear in free product concentration, neglecting finite occupancy/saturation of inhibitory binding to enzyme.
plan.baseline_assumption: All product rebinding events to free enzyme obey elementary bimolecular mass action with a constant association coefficient, regardless of accumulated product level and inhibitory site occupancy.
plan.scientific_mechanism: Saturable product inhibition of enzyme activity due to finite inhibitory binding capacity, causing diminishing incremental inhibition at high product concentration.
plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to relax the idealized assumption that product inhibition strength keeps increasing proportionally to free product over the full trajectory. In many enzyme systems, inhibitory binding has a finite occupancy scale, so once product becomes comparable to that scale, additional product causes smaller marginal loss of catalytic throughput. The parent target mapping from observed states to dP_dt is effectively controlled by one linear-in-P inhibition branch through free enzyme sequestration. Holding E_total and kinetic constants fixed while varying initial substrate concentration changes how far P rises during the run. Under those admissible conditions, the parent with one shared parameter set cannot simultaneously match both early-time near-linear inhibition when P is small and late/high-substrate flattening of inhibition when P becomes large, because its inhibitory contribution keeps growing proportionally with P. The child changes the target mapping itself, not only auxiliary trajectories: for the same observed C, EP, and P, dP_dt would decline less steeply with further increases in large P than in the parent. This contrast is scientifically visible only when the experiment reaches moderate-to-high product levels; if P stays low throughout, the refinement is weak and the parent is recovered approximately.

plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to relax the parent's one-channel inhibition assumption. The current target mapping from observed states to dP_dt has a single inhibitory pathway: P removes free enzyme into EP, which lowers future formation of C, but once C exists the output branch remains exactly k_cat*C. Varying product accumulation while holding E_total and the parent kinetic constants fixed therefore gives only one-phase saturation in the rate reduction. In many enzyme systems, product inhibition is mixed rather than purely competitive, so rising P can depress catalytic turnover of already bound substrate as well. This changes the scored target mapping directly, not merely auxiliary trajectories, because dP_dt at the same observed C can differ depending on P. The contrast is observable under the existing initial-condition protocol when substrate is initially abundant, C rises transiently, and P later accumulates into the inhibition range: the child predicts stronger downward curvature, earlier peak suppression, or a lower late transient rate than the parent can achieve with one shared parameter set. The effect weakens when P remains far below K_I_P or after C is nearly exhausted, so those limitations should be stated honestly.

plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to relax the parent's fixed-environment assumption inside the catalytic inhibition term rather than add a wholly new species. The parent target mapping has a fixed product-only suppression shape: once C and P are known, the catalytic part of dP_dt is fixed, so any two observations with the same C and P must have the same turnover contribution regardless of S. In a closed batch reaction, however, substrate systematically changes from high to low while product rises, and product inhibition of catalysis can plausibly depend on the substrate environment because substrate occupancy or substrate-rich conformations can buffer product's inhibitory effect. The child therefore changes the response from a separable P-only suppression to a joint S-P interaction in the catalytic factor. Holding E_total and all other conditions fixed, compare periods where P is in the inhibitory range near K_I_cat but S is still high versus later when S is depleted: the child predicts a steeper late-phase decline in dP_dt/C than the parent because the same product burden inhibits more strongly at low S. This is a direct change to the scored target mapping, not merely to auxiliary trajectories, since dP_dt itself at given observed S,C,P changes. The mechanism is admissible without new degrees of freedom because S is already a tracked state. A single refit of existing parent parameters cannot reproduce this contrast across such conditions: changing k_cat, K_I_cat, or n_I_cat only reshapes inhibition as a function of P globally, but cannot make inhibition weak at high S and strong at low S when P and C are otherwise comparable.

response_change.parent_relation: The catalytic term depends only on accumulated product through k_cat*C/(1 + (P/K_I_cat)**n_I_cat), so at fixed P and C the instantaneous product-formation contribution is independent of substrate level S.
response_change.child_relation: Retain product suppression but let direct turnover suppression depend jointly on product accumulation and substrate occupancy, so that at the same P and C the effective catalytic inhibition weakens when S is high and strengthens as S becomes depleted.
response_change.observable_effect: During late transient and depletion phases, two times with similar P but different S can show different dP_dt/C in the child, whereas the parent predicts the same value once C and P are fixed.

diagnostic_groups.name: prod_load
diagnostic_groups.role: scale of direct product-mediated catalytic suppression

diagnostic_groups.name: substrate_occupancy
diagnostic_groups.role: available substrate level governing whether product acts under substrate-rich or substrate-poor conditions

diagnostic_groups.name: normalized_turnover
diagnostic_groups.role: parent catalytic contribution to dP_dt for comparison against a substrate-modulated child law

contract.activation_condition: Observable when product has accumulated to P comparable to K_I_cat and substrate is no longer overwhelmingly abundant, so product suppression is active while S still varies substantially along the trajectory.
contract.train_hidden_contrast: In training, early high-S portions and later lower-S portions already coexist on one batch trajectory; the same product level can be encountered with different substrate availability across trajectories or neighboring times, and holdout extends this contrast deeper into depletion where the substrate dependence of inhibition is stronger.
contract.continuation_path: Recover the parent law in the limit that substrate modulation of catalytic inhibition vanishes, e.g. a large substrate-protection scale or zero coupling strength so the turnover term depends only on P again.
contract.domain_mechanism: substrate-dependent direct product inhibition of catalytic turnover
contract.scientific_mechanism: Substrate-dependent mixed inhibition of catalysis: accumulated product suppresses turnover less strongly when substrate is abundant, consistent with partial substrate protection of the catalytic conformation or reduced access of inhibitory product effects under substrate-rich conditions.
contract.difficulty_rationale: This embedding is harder than a coefficient-only correction because it changes the catalytic response from a product-only suppression curve into a joint S-P law, so no single global retuning of k_cat, K_I_cat, or n_I_cat can reproduce different inhibition strengths at the same P and C across varying substrate environments.
contract.assumption_before: All elementary kinetic coefficients remain constant during the trajectory, specifically the product-suppressed catalytic efficiency depends only on P and not on the contemporaneous substrate environment.
contract.assumption_after: Direct product-mediated catalytic suppression is buffered by substrate abundance through a substrate-dependent effective inhibition scale.
contract.before_fragment: k_cat*C/(1 + (P/K_I_cat)**n_I_cat) - k_on_P*(E_total - C - EP)*P/(1 + P/K_I_P) + k_off_P*EP
contract.after_fragment: k_cat*C/(1 + (P/(K_I_cat*(1 + S/K_S_protect)))**n_I_cat) - k_on_P*(E_total - C - EP)*P/(1 + P/K_I_P) + k_off_P*EP
contract.parent_reduction: The parent is recovered in the limit K_S_protect -> oo, which removes substrate protection and restores the original product-only inhibition factor.
contract.observable_signature: Relative turnover dP_dt/C is no longer a function of P alone after subtracting the EP exchange terms; when P is in the inhibitory range near K_I_cat, higher S shifts suppression onset to larger P, so late low-S portions of the batch show stronger catalytic depression than earlier high-S portions even at similar P and C.
contract.shortcut_blocked: A single parent parameter set cannot reproduce this because the parent catalytic contribution is separable from S once C and P are given. Retuning k_cat rescales all catalytic fluxes, while retuning K_I_cat or n_I_cat only changes the global P-response shape; none can make inhibition weak at high S and strong at low S for otherwise comparable P and C across the admissible trajectory segment.

range_suggestions.K_S_protect: positive; on the order of the substrate concentration range where substrate-rich conditions begin to noticeably buffer direct product-mediated catalytic suppression
